newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended lower in featureless conditions. Slow physical demand undermined sentiment. March finished the session at $302.30 per tonne, down $1.90 from Thursday's close. May gave up $2.0 to close at $301.10.

In New York raw sugar futures closed lower across the board in subdued activity. Most active March lost 8 points to close at 10.64 cents/lb while May closed 9 points lower at 10.74 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 6 and 7 points. The market showed little reaction to the USDA cancelling the supplementary 200,000 tonne sugar import quota. However, this could put prices under pressure on Monday.

UNITED STATES - In its latest world supply demand report the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) estimated that US sugar stocks at the end of fiscal 1997 (October/September 1996/97) will reach 1.587 million tons, raw value, or 15.6 per cent of forecast total use, a key figure in setting the import quota. At the start of fiscal 1997, USDA allocated 1.7 million tonnes of imports with adjustments to be considered in January, March and May. If the stocks ratio is 15.5 per cent or less on the review date, the quota automatically goes up 200,000 tonnes. If it is higher, the tranche is cancelled. Beginning stocks are put at a marginally higher figure than in the December estimate because of revisions in 1995/96 data. Sugar production in 1996/97 is up slightly from last month, with all of the change in cane sugar. Processing of Louisiana sugar cane was completed on January 7, with sugar production reaching an estimated 1.045 million short tons. Production forecasts for Texas - affected by drought - and Hawaii were lowered. Forecast sugar deliveries remained unchanged at last month's figure of 9.9 million tons, sharply up for the second straight year.

CHINA - Sugar production in December 1996 reached 1.576 million tonnes, raw value, slightly up from the 1.510 million tonnes produced the same month the previous year. That brought total production from domestically grown beet and cane since the beginning of 1996/97 (September/August) up to 2.262 million tonnes, raw value, which compares to 1.941 million tonnes produced the same year-ago period. Total production in crop year 1995/96 rose to 6.8 million tonnes, up from 5.9 million tonnes produced in 1994/95.

UNITED KINGDOM - Sugar imports from third countries in November 1996 amounted 97,732 tonnes, raw value, which brought cumulative imports in the first two months of 1996/97 (October/November) up to 226,767 tonnes. Total imports in 1995/96 (October/September) reached 1.237 million tonnes against 1.356 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in October/November 1996 were Mauritius with 119,213 tonnes raws, Guyana with 64,500 tonnes and Fiji with 39,900 tonnes. Sugar exports to third countries in November 1996 amounted to 12,699 tonnes which brought cumulative exports in October/November 1996 up to 38,582 tonnes. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 324,415 tonnes against 465,621 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in October/November 1996 were Israel with 15,551 tonnes whites and Norway with 7,925 tonnes.

FRANCE - Sugar consumption in August 1996 reached 169,249 tonnes, raw value, sharply down from the 224,051 tonnes in July 1996 and also below the 182,928 tonnes in August 1995. This brought cumulative consumption in the first eleven months of 1995/96 (October/August) up to 1.984 million tonnes, up from last year's 1.960 million tonnes. Total consumption in 1994/95 reached 2.184 million tonnes compared to 2.208 million tonnes in 1993/94.
